title: Moai: the British Museum’s account of removal, return requests and collaboration
author: British Museum

notes.text: Reviewed on 3 October 2026 for the proposed exhibition A Short History of Taking Things and Keeping Them. Relevant sections: How did the objects come to the British Museum?; What has been requested?; Status of discussions; The British Museum's position. The page describes removal, transfer through the Admiralty and Queen Victoria, the July 2018 return request and subsequent collaborations. It acknowledges the impact of removal and argues for the educational significance of London display. These are the Museum's accounts and positions, not evidence of Rapanui consent or a final return decision. Its name translations must remain attributed. No publication date is established. The reviewed SingleFile copy remains in private staging: no licence for redistributing the complete page and embedded media was established. The Museum's copyright policy explicitly says its Creative Commons licence does not cover all website content. Source registration and links are complete; no new object claims or public facsimile are supplied in this source-only pass.
